header.title: How to Properly Vent a Kitchen Range Exhaust Hood
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to properly vent a kitchen range exhaust hood, covering exit ventilation, ductwork installation, and hood mounting.

steps.description: This step explains the options for venting an exhaust hood, emphasizing the importance of venting to the outside to prevent fire hazards.
actions: Choose between ceiling or wall installation for exhaust venting.
Consider range location to determine venting option (attic or wall).
Do not vent into the wall or attic.
Run the exhaust fan duct to the outside of the house.

steps.description: This step involves marking, cutting, and running ductwork for the vent hood exhaust.
actions: Cover the hole that you are not using for exhaust
Secure the hood to its final positioning to mark the location of the vent duct
Remove the hood
Cut a hole in the wall or ceiling
Make guide holes
Complete the circle with a saw
Go into the attic if you chose a ceiling exit
Run the duct from the hole to an external wall or your roof
Mark where you are going to cut the second hole for exiting from the house
Use stiff or flex ducting
Ensure the duct protrudes a little out both the ceiling and the exit point
Cover the exit with a vent cap/cover
Caulk around the edges

steps.description: This step involves installing the vent hood, connecting its components, wiring it, and testing its functionality.
actions: Connect the vent hood using screws and anchors
Caulk around the seams between the vent hood and the ceiling
Install the fan
Install the filter
Install the light kit
Hook up all the wiring, black to black, white to white, and green to green (or copper)
Use wire nuts to cover the loose ends of the wires
Secure the wires under the electrical component cover
Turn on the vent hood
Verify the lights and fan work
Verify there are no leaks in the duct
Verify the exhaust is going out through the exit duct
